finding: Partial. The printed bullet asserts intrinsic nuclear Fréchet local and global norm-one theta isotypes, jointly continuous left translation by the full groups, and convolution actions. Lean proves the local translation portion for F = ℚ, S = {∞}, retaining the actual quotient by the kernel of the S-unit theta sum and the actual group quotient J = ℝˣ/im(ℤˣ) with their respective quotient topologies. The full J action is jointly continuous and by complex continuous linear maps, with evaluation on any representative f at u⁻¹x given by the original unweighted two-term theta sum. It proves that the norm-one subgroup is trivial; mathematically in this case its only character gives the full local theta quotient, since the homogeneous average is multiplication by a positive Haar mass and has the same kernel. The existing Masullo.rationalRealThetaEquiv and Masullo.rationalRealThetaQuotient_frechet give the even Schwartz model and the intrinsic Fréchet properties (see rational-real-theta-quotient.md). The weighted dilation is used only after removing its scalar weight. The printed (5.2.3.9) uses the conjugated character on the inverse-translation operator; inversion gives the same-character operator P_ω in the homogeneous theta identity, not P_(conj ω) as printed in the proof of (5.2.3.15). Idempotence additionally requires division by the Haar mass if it is not one; that is separate from character conjugation. The code does not prove the general homogeneous-isotype identification or its transition diagrams, local or global nuclearity, the local result for other F or larger S, the global result, or the Pettis and convolution steps even in the real specialization.
retry: Provide jointly continuous representative translation on a compatible Schwartz–Bruhat LF stage model with the actual kernel and open quotient maps, then a Pettis-averaging and quotient-to-closed-isotype theorem for compact norm-one actions with the same-character convention and compatible Haar measures. For the general Fréchet and nuclear steps, formalize the intrinsic-topology local closed embedding (or an alternative with closed range) and nuclearity/permanence, and prove the finite-stage topological isomorphisms and eventual global surjectivity under the Picard and ramification hypotheses. To obtain convolution, construct the compactly supported orbit Pettis integrals in those spaces, with compact-parameter seminorm bounds and the scalar Fubini identity for composition. For the real case alone, a nuclearity theorem for even real-line Schwartz space and that compact-support integration interface would extend the checked endpoint.
